unit.why: A narrative about R. Abraham Joshua Heschel of Apta as rabbi of Kolbuszow being unknowingly bribed, framed by a homily on 'even a perfect tzaddik who takes a bribe'.
unit.boundary_note: trailing 'מענין שידוך' is the heading of the next division

stories.start_quote: והדרש אפילו צדיק גמור ונוטל שוחד
stories.end_quote: ובלי ידיעה כלל קיבל שוחד נסתלף דבריו
stories.summary_en: As young rabbi of Kolbuszow, the Apter Rav found his judgment bending toward corrupt judges after a litigant secretly hid gold coins in his Rosh Hodesh garment; he wept, delayed the verdict, found the coins, made the man confess and return them, and drew the lesson that even a perfect tzaddik is swayed by an unknowing bribe.
